Use N/A for absent or partial capabilities, material semantic gaps, or cases without a pragmatic faithful interface.

The implementation uses a typed arena and source-backed numeric adapters rather than Ruby's open object runtime, while preserving the material logic available to cop, node-pattern, traversal, and correction consumers.
known_workarounds: Current higher-level RuboCop behavior uses ruby-prism plus crates/rustocop/src/rubocop/ast/node/core.rs, whose typed Ast, NodeRef, and NodeValue model implements the parser-shaped operations Rustocop actually consumes. Consumers requiring Ruby's open subclass or post-construction mutation semantics need an explicit consumer-scoped adapter or a Ruby VM boundary and must not treat that typed model as AST::Node equivalence.

Until the numeric child model is made value-preserving, consumers that compare integer, float, rational, or complex literals must derive Ruby-compatible semantic values from the source-backed numeric helpers instead of relying on NodeValue or NodeRef::structurally_equal.

The numeric workaround above was incorporated into NodeRef::structurally_equal and rubocop_hash_equivalent during the consumer-capability remediation, so callers now receive source-backed Ruby numeric semantics through the canonical comparison API.
